name: Fiji

findings.summary: Reporting on Telstra's 2022 Digicel Pacific acquisition said Digicel's 3G and 4G networks across its five markets, including Fiji, run on Huawei equipment that Telstra would keep until future refreshes.
findings.analyst_inference: Only ChannelNews names Fiji; PINA covers Digicel Pacific generally (PNG-based) and reports Telstra's pledge to remove Huawei gear at the next refresh, which is a statement of intent, not yet a reversal. Neither source is S1/S2, so not corroborated. FJI-002 (Nokia upgrade, 2024) may be that refresh, but no source confirms Huawei kit was removed in Fiji.

findings.summary: Digicel Fiji said it is working with Nokia to upgrade cell sites nationwide using Nokia's AirScale equipment in preparation for 5G; Digicel and Vodafone Fiji launched first-phase 5G in September 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Nokia (Finland) is the equipment vendor. Tier 3: a vendor engagement is reported but no contract value. DCD confirms the 5G launch but names no vendor, so tier 5 is not coded. Possibly the Huawei swap Telstra promised (FJI-001); not stated by any source, so no reversal coded.

findings.summary: Google's Bulikula and Tabua subsea cables, part of its South/Central Pacific Connect programme, landed at FINTEL's Vatuwaqa station in Suva in January 2025, with FINTEL providing landing facilities and cable management.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us: Google owns the systems; the cable manufacturer is not named, so the equipment-vendor rule cannot be applied and owner control is used instead; reviewer call. Tier 4 (landed, not confirmed in service). DCD 2023 covers the Tabua announcement only.

findings.summary: Fiji's Deputy Prime Minister said Google would invest about US$200 million in a data centre in Fiji alongside new international cables; no location, specification or timeline was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: a ministerial statement relayed from a fijivillage interview, with no confirmation from Google in the sources seen. Pole us assumes Google would own and operate the facility.

findings.controller: PRC Ministry of Public Security (donor; equipment vendor not named)
findings.summary: China's Ministry of Public Security donated police vehicles, drones, vehicle conference systems and servers linking CCTV cameras to the police monitoring network to Fiji Police, worth about US$730,000 at the time.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc because the PRC state supplied the kit; the server and CCTV equipment vendor is not named, so this is a reviewer call. Tier 5 because the handover was completed; whether the servers are still in use is unconfirmed. Small value, but it touches the police CCTV network.

findings.controller: Unknown (camera and platform vendor not named)
findings.summary: Under its Safe City Project, Fiji Police contracted Telecom Fiji for fibre and CCTV along the Suva–Nausori corridor, with feeds monitored at police command centres; by August 2026, 97 of 230 planned cameras were working, and facial recognition was planned.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no source names the camera, analytics or facial-recognition vendor. Telecom Fiji (state-linked, domestic) is the integrator and connectivity supplier, not documented as the equipment vendor. Tier 5 for the partial operation in Suva. Not corroborated because there is no S1/S2 source (Telecom Fiji's own release counted as S4).

Who supplies the cameras, video platform and facial recognition for the Fiji Police Safe City Project, and who funds it?
